name: Hare Krishna Books
description:
Hare Krishna Books with its branches located all over the world was Started in 1944 with a Back to Godhead magazine by AC Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada.

Along with our other Hare Krishna centers worldwide & with our own multinational publishing house, Bhakti Vedanta Book Trust (BBT) founded in 1972 we have become the world’s largest publisher of Indian scriptures in more than 90 languages.

Bhagavad Gita as it is by Swami Prabhupada has sold over 26 million copies so far & has become the largest-selling edition of the Gita in the world & the standard reference edition of the Gita worldwide.

Now you can place an order for these Indian wisdom books at a reasonable rate through this online store in any part of the world.

featured_reviews.name: Nida Sayed Kadri
featured_reviews.review_text:
Misleading pricing, zero customer service, and shockingly rude behaviour — absolutely not worth the visit.

I visited this shop to purchase (not rent) a complete book series and clearly explained my requirement at the very start. The owner initially seemed pleased when he heard I wanted to buy. Instead of helping, he asked me to search through a stack of books and said he would remove the set if I found it.

I found one part of the series myself and asked him to look for the remaining books. He completely ignored the request. When I asked for the price of the entire set, he quoted an amount which I felt was reasonable for a second-hand paperback. However, when I again asked for the remaining books, he suddenly said that price was for just one book, not the full set.

I calmly mentioned that a brand-new set online costs one-fourth of what he was asking for a single second-hand copy. That’s when things turned ugly. He got irritated, raised his voice, and when I politely asked why the pricing was so high, he became openly aggressive and started yelling.

He even accused me of “wasting his effort” saying “itni mehnat karayi, kaam karwaya ab book nahi leni” — which is absurd, considering I was there for barely 5 minutes and had found the book myself from the first stack. Neither he nor his staff made any effort to help.

I finally told him that he needs to learn basic manners while dealing with customers.

If this shop believes that once a book is shown, purchasing is mandatory, then they should put up a clear sign outside. Until then, be prepared for rude behaviour, misleading pricing, and zero customer courtesy.

featured_reviews.name: Kusal Rai
featured_reviews.review_text: Tucked away in an aesthetic corner of South Bombay, this bookstore is a true haven for book lovers. With its charming atmosphere and thoughtfully curated shelves, it offers an impressive range of genres that caters to every kind of reader. Whether you’re hunting for a classic, exploring contemporary fiction, or diving into niche subjects, this place makes browsing feel like an experience rather than just a visit. featured_reviews.name: Anil Bishnoi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ashish Book Centre, tucked away near the bustling CSMT Railway Station in Fort, is nothing short of a paradise for true book lovers. In a city that’s always racing against time, this bookstore feels like a quiet, timeless refuge where stories patiently wait to be discovered.

What makes Ashish Book Centre truly special is its incredible collection. From rare second-hand classics and academic textbooks to novels, competitive exam guides, and out-of-print treasures—you never know what gem you’ll stumble upon. Browsing through the shelves feels like going on a literary treasure hunt, and every visit brings a new surprise.

The owners and staff are extremely knowledgeable and helpful. They don’t just sell books; they understand them. Whether you walk in with a specific title in mind or just a vague idea of what you want to read, they guide you with genuine enthusiasm and honesty. Their passion for books is infectious.

Another big win is the affordability. Ashish Book Centre proves that great reading doesn’t have to be expensive. Students, avid readers, and collectors alike will appreciate the fair pricing and excellent condition of the books.

Located in the heart of Fort, just a stone’s throw from CSMT, it’s incredibly convenient and perfectly placed for a spontaneous visit after work or college. Despite the chaos outside, the store offers a calm, almost nostalgic vibe that reminds you why physical bookstores still matter.

If you love books, value knowledge, or simply enjoy the charm of old-school bookstores, Ashish Book Centre is an absolute must-visit. It’s not just a shop—it’s an experience, a legacy, and a reminder that the love for reading is very much alive in Mumbai. 📚
